cards.explanation: The answer is out to meet Asa. Verse 1 says the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded, and verse 2 says he went out to meet Asa, Judah's king. And then he says, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin.”

The answer is when they are with Him. Azariah says, “The LORD is with you when you are with Him.” Notice it's not about what Judah has, but about being with Him. That's the whole sentence, friends, and it's a good one to hang on the fridge.

The answer is False. Azariah says, “If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.” Two roads, both clearly marked. I like a sign that tells you the truth up front.

The answer is that they sought the LORD and found Him. Verse 4 says, “But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.” They turned to the LORD in their distress, and He was found by them. That's exactly what Azariah promised in verse 2.

The answer is True. It's right there in verse 6: “…for God afflicted them with all kinds of adversity.” It comes right after nation was crushed by nation, and city by city. This is one of the heavy parts of Azariah's message, friends, so it deserves a quiet moment.

The answer is courage. Verse 8 says, “When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet, he took courage…” Azariah told him to be strong, and Asa took it to heart. And then he got busy.

The answer is idols. Verse 8 says Asa “…removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin…” He also removed them from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. Courage went straight to work, friends.

The answer is the altar of the LORD. Verse 8 says, “He then restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD’s temple.” First the idols go out, then the altar is set right. Asa cleans the house and fixes what matters.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says, “…for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.” They saw that the LORD his God was with him, and they came. Verse 9 also says Asa assembled all Judah and Benjamin, along with those from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had settled among them.

The answer is the plunder they brought back. Verse 11 says they sacrificed the seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep “…from all the plunder they had brought back.” Those numbers aren't small, friends. And it shows what they did with what they carried home.

The answer is with all their heart and soul. Verse 12 says they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, “…with all their heart and soul.” That's all in, nothing held back. It matches what Azariah told them about seeking Him.

The answer is that they would be put to death. Verse 13 says, “…whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death…” That's a heavy line, friends, and I won't pretend it isn't. It shows how seriously they took the covenant they had just made.

The answer is False. Verse 13 says whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, would be put to death, “…whether young or old, man or woman.” The text doesn't limit it to the men. It's a heavy verse, but the wording is clear.

The answer is rejoiced. Verse 15 says, “And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart.” After the shouting, trumpets and rams' horns, joy fits. And it says all Judah, so nobody was sitting this one out.

The answer is rest on every side. Verse 15 says, “So the LORD gave them rest on every side.” They sought Him earnestly, and He was found by them, just like Azariah said. Rest on every side is a gift any of us could use, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 16 says Asa removed Maacah, his grandmother, from her position as queen mother “…because she had made a detestable Asherah pole.” No plot is mentioned. I think that was a hard thing for a king to do in his own family.

The answer is False. Asa did clear idols out, but verse 17 says, “The high places were not removed from Israel…” The text gives us both parts, the good work and what was left standing. So saying the high places were removed doesn't match the text.

The answer is fully devoted all his days. Verse 17 says, “…Asa’s heart was fully devoted all his days.” The high places were still standing, and the text tells us this about his heart anyway. It's one sentence, friends, and it's a lovely one.
The answer is thirty-fifth. Verse 19 says, “And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.” Quiet right up until that year of his reign. That's a lot of peaceful batches, friends.
